name: Water held between bars
brief:
`heights[i]` is the height of a bar of width 1. After rain, water sits in the dips between taller bars. Return how many units of water the bars hold. Water that could run off either end is not held.

Write `trapped_water(heights)`.

Example. For `heights = [3, 1, 3]` the middle column holds 2 units between two walls of 3, so the answer is 2.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 200{,}000$ bars, each at least 0 high.
$O(n)$ time is the target. Scanning for walls at every bar is too slow.
All tests share a 5-second time limit.
hint: Water over a bar rises to the lower of its two walls. Walk inward from both ends and move the side with the lower wall.

examples.note: The bars 0, 2 and 0 sit under a level of 3. They hold 3, 1 and 3 units, so 7.
The middle bar is 1 high between two bars of 3, so it holds 2.

how: There are 11 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: The lower end bar limits the water at its side, whatever lies between the ends.
So the side with the lower bar can be settled using only the tallest bar it has met.
Each bar is visited once, so the work is $O(n)$.
